Prescription-only fixed-dose combination. Components – Diclofenac Diethylamine

(topical): Non-prescription (OTC) for 1.16% gel in many markets; prescription per Indian label; Methyl Salicylate (topical): Topical ingredient (pharmacopoeial); Menthol (topical): Topical ingredient (pharmacopoeial); Linseed Oil (topical): Topical excipient/ingredient

Diclofenac Diethylamine (topical): The diethylamine salt was developed to improve skin penetration of diclofenac in gel formulations. First approval/introduction: Topical emulgel introduced 1985 (Ciba-Geigy). Methyl Salicylate (topical): Naturally present in wintergreen (Gaultheria procumbens); 5 mL of pure oil is equivalent to ~7 g of aspirin and is highly toxic if ingested. First approval/introduction: Oil of wintergreen; synthetic product since 1886. Menthol (topical): Obtained from Mentha arvensis (cornmint) oil or synthesised; India is the world's largest producer. First approval/introduction: Pharmacopoeial (IP/BP/USP). Linseed Oil (topical): Flaxseed oil used as an emollient base in topical analgesic preparations. First approval/introduction: Pharmacopoeial (BP).
Diclofenac diethylamine 1.16% + Methyl salicylate 10% + Menthol 5% + Linseed oil
Topical diclofenac reduces local inflammation; methyl salicylate and menthol are counter-irritants providing rapid warming/cooling relief; linseed oil acts as an emollient vehicle aiding penetration.

Diclofenac Diethylamine (topical) Penetrates skin to inflamed soft tissues and joints where it inhibits prostaglandin synthesis, giving local analgesic and anti-inflammatory action with low systemic exposure (~6% of oral). Receptor / target profile: Local COX inhibition in synovium and soft tissue.

Methyl Salicylate (topical) Produces local vasodilation and counter-irritant warmth; partly absorbed and hydrolysed to salicylic acid giving local analgesia. Receptor / target profile: Counter-irritant producing local hyperaemia; hydrolysed salicylate gives local anti-inflammatory activity.

Menthol (topical) Activates TRPM8 cold receptors producing a cooling sensation and counter-irritant analgesia; mild local anaesthetic effect. Receptor / target profile: Activates TRPM8 cold receptors (cooling sensation) and kappa-opioid receptors; weak local anaesthetic.

Linseed Oil (topical) Rich in alpha-linolenic acid; acts as an emollient base aiding skin penetration of active ingredients and has mild anti-inflammatory activity. Receptor / target profile: Emollient vehicle; alpha-linolenic acid has mild local anti-inflammatory activity.
Summary: Systemic absorption ~6% of an equivalent oral dose; local tissue concentrations achieved.

Diclofenac Diethylamine (topical): Unlikely with topical use; accidental ingestion – treat as NSAID overdose. Methyl Salicylate (topical): Ingestion is highly toxic (salicylism) – emergency care. Menthol (topical): Ingestion – CNS depression; supportive care. Linseed Oil (topical): Not applicable.
Cochrane review (Derry et al., 2015) – topical diclofenac effective for acute musculoskeletal pain (NNT ~2–4 for gel formulations).

Store below 30°C in a dry place, protected from light and moisture. Keep out of the reach of children. Do not use after the expiry date.
